title: Week 28 Mastery Quiz · Climate, Resources, and Environmental Justice

questions.question: The Paris Agreement Article 4 concerns nationally determined contributions. What distinction matters in a student evidence table?
options: A stated national target is not the same as measured emissions reductions or achieved outcomes.
All contributions are identical legal emission caps.
Submitting a target proves delivery.
Every target covers the same economic sectors.
questions.explanation: A stated national target is not the same as measured emissions reductions or achieved outcomes.

questions.question: Fictional coastal districts face identical storm exposure but different household incomes and evacuation access. Which comparison best captures climate justice?
options: Exposure alone proves equal risk.
Physical hazard plus unequal vulnerability, adaptation resources and exposure to harm.
Income cannot affect resilience.
Both districts necessarily have identical losses.
questions.explanation: Physical hazard plus unequal vulnerability, adaptation resources and exposure to harm.

questions.question: A policy reduces average emissions but causes steep heating-cost increases among low-income households. What evidence should an evaluation include?
options: Aggregate reductions prove everyone benefits equally.
Energy affordability has no policy relevance.
Carbon effects alongside distributional costs, support measures and feasible alternatives.
Mitigation and equity cannot be studied together.
questions.explanation: Carbon effects alongside distributional costs, support measures and feasible alternatives.

questions.question: A fictional region reports 15% more rainfall but 30% higher flood losses. What interpretation is most defensible?
options: Rainfall alone accounts for every dollar lost.
Any increase proves one policy caused flooding.
Damage data cannot be related to rainfall.
Losses can reflect precipitation, exposed assets, land-use decisions and protective capacity together.
questions.explanation: Losses can reflect precipitation, exposed assets, land-use decisions and protective capacity together.

questions.question: A national adaptation plan lists new seawalls but no maintenance or ecological impacts. Which appraisal is stronger?
options: Consider life-cycle costs, affected communities, ecosystem effects and alternative protections.
Construction alone guarantees long-term resilience.
Ecological effects cannot be observed.
All shoreline communities face equal risk.
questions.explanation: Consider life-cycle costs, affected communities, ecosystem effects and alternative protections.

questions.question: A mining proposal cites energy-transition benefits but excludes Indigenous communities from consultation records. Which question needs investigation?
options: Clean-energy goals automatically waive procedural rights.
Applicable consultation rights, land tenure, distribution of harms and evidence of meaningful participation.
Consultation is equivalent to a press notice.
A national benefit estimate records each local impact.
questions.explanation: Applicable consultation rights, land tenure, distribution of harms and evidence of meaningful participation.

questions.question: Two states publish different climate baselines when announcing percentage cuts. What calculation issue is central?
options: Percent cuts are directly comparable without baselines.
Only population determines the baseline.
The starting year, emissions inventory, sector coverage and absolute totals determine comparability.
Different baselines prove dishonesty.
questions.explanation: The starting year, emissions inventory, sector coverage and absolute totals determine comparability.

questions.question: A carbon-pricing scheme reports revenue but no emissions baseline. What outcome claim is unsupported?
options: The government collected revenue.
Pricing policy was implemented.
Revenue can be reported in currency.
Its emissions-reduction effect cannot be inferred from revenue collection alone.
questions.explanation: Its emissions-reduction effect cannot be inferred from revenue collection alone.

questions.question: A source cites the Paris Agreement temperature objective as proof that current policy will achieve it. What distinction is essential?
options: International goals and actual global trajectories require different evidence and implementation analysis.
Adoption automatically guarantees outcomes.
National inventories are unnecessary.
Targets cannot be evaluated.
questions.explanation: International goals and actual global trajectories require different evidence and implementation analysis.

questions.question: A government claims one drought caused by climate change without supporting attribution research. What should a cautious assessment say?
options: Every drought has identical causes.
Assess long-term trends, event attribution evidence, exposure and uncertainty before assigning a singular cause.
One event alone measures global warming.
Climate science excludes natural variability.
questions.explanation: Assess long-term trends, event attribution evidence, exposure and uncertainty before assigning a singular cause.

shortResponse: How can political institutions govern environmental risks that cross borders, generations, and unequal communities?
rubric: 10 points: precise claim (2), accurate concepts (2), two specific pieces of evidence (2), reasoning (2), counterargument or limitation (1), revision condition (1).
